overall_reason: The product copy and spec block are specific (7.4 oz, 34 mm stack, 8 mm drop, Gel-02 pods) and the type has a point of view, but the hero is a clip-art sneaker on a blurred peach radial glow, the chrome is the warm-paper kit (cream page, terracotta accent, tracked mono caps with middot chains, italic accent words, corner 'stamps'), and the brand is a placeholder.

findings.evidence: The product, the only reason for the email, is a hand-drawn inline SVG shoe (flat orange upper, five curved strokes, a white flash, a bracket for a sole) floating on a CSS radial-gradient glow. T-COVER-TEXT: with text hidden this reads as a generic shoe icon, not the Axis Pro in 'Ember Flare' and its 'painterly flame-knit upper' that the copy describes.
findings.before: Inline SVG sneaker drawing on radial-gradient background
findings.after: A real product photograph of the Ember Flare colourway as a hosted at 600px email width with alt text [DATA NEEDED: product photography]
findings.why: A launch email has to show the product; a schematic drawing contradicts 'painterly flame-knit' and reads as a placeholder.

findings.where: masthead, hero stamps, eyebrow, spec labels
findings.evidence: Warm-paper family tells the sweep could only partly measure: cream #f4efe7 page, terracotta #d8482b accent, italic accent words ('AXIS PRO.', 'Ember Flare'), and tracked mono caps with middot chains on every label: 'EST · 2024', '— SPORT TEST', '— EMBER FLARE', 'DROP 04 · 04—2026', 'NEW · MAX-CUSHION TRAINER · EMBER FLARE', 'SPECIFICATIONS · WOMEN'S'. T-DELETION: the three hero corner stamps and 'EST · 2024' carry no fact the reader needs.
findings.after: Keep one label (the eyebrow, rewritten as a fact like 'Ships 4 April'); drop the stamps and EST badge
findings.why: Three or more tells of one look family on one surface read as the default, not a brand choice.

findings.where: brand name 'SPORT TEST' (masthead, hero stamp, footer)
findings.evidence: The sender brand is 'SPORT TEST', a test placeholder, repeated three times including '© 2026 SPORT TEST'; every link (nav, CTA, Unsubscribe, View in browser) is href '#'.
findings.after: [DATA NEEDED: real brand name and tracked URLs]; a working unsubscribe link is required before send
findings.why: Placeholder residue at ship; a dead unsubscribe link is also a legal problem for marketing email.

findings.where: h1 'MEET THE AXIS PRO. A SNEAKER THAT RUNS.'
findings.evidence: T-THREE-LINE: 'A sneaker that runs' is not falsifiable and fits any running shoe (T-RIVAL-NAME: swap in any brand's trainer and it holds). The body line 'softer underfoot, louder on the outside' is the stock antithesis pair.
findings.after: Use a spec as the claim: 'Meet the Axis Pro. 34 mm of gel under your heel.'
findings.why: The specs are the specific material; the headline should use them.

findings.evidence: dom-800.json: layout is divs/sections with CSS aspect-ratio, radial gradients, an @media query and an inline . Gmail and Outlook strip SVG and most of this CSS, so the hero and layout will not render as captured.
findings.before: div layout + inline SVG + CSS gradients
findings.after: Table-based 600px layout with inline styles and a hosted raster hero image
findings.why: An email's design is what the client renders; this capture shows a browser-only version.

strengths: The spec block is real product information with units and qualifiers ('34MM max-cushion stack at the heel', '8MM heel-to-toe drop for low-impact landing'); keep it and make it the lead.
Single clear CTA ('Shop the Axis Pro') and a compliant footer structure with address, unsubscribe and view-in-browser.
not_investigated: Rendering in real email clients (only a browser capture exists); preheader text not present in the DOM capture.
